g.title: OX05DepthOrdering
g.text: OX-05 | MAKE FIRST CITY DEPTH ORDER ENFORCEABLE
Behavior board • cycle 144 • see cycle plan for approval status and fingerprints

g.title: cluster_stack
g.text: PROPOSED VIEW INTO THE WORLD • Background sublayers, then Middle-Ground sublayers, then Foreground sublayers

g.title: input
g.text: ACTIVE CATALOG • ONE SELECTED INSTANT
OX-03 supplies one First City composition decision set.
OX-04 evidence, support, and source-time semantics remain unchanged.

g.title: render
g.text: EXISTING FIRST CITY RENDER PATH
FirstCityComposition.layerOrder is consumed by the catalog renderer.
The reading fallback preserves the same city draw sequence.

g.title: input->render
g.text: compose once; preserve selected time

g.title: background
g.text: BACKGROUND • far world layers
OUTER_SPACE → STARS → TIME_CUE (SUN) → LUNAR_CUE (MOON)
Then BACKGROUND_CLOUDS → BACKGROUND_ARCHITECTURE
Sun is farther than Moon; only the outer-space backdrop and stars sit behind the celestial field

g.title: render->background
g.text: classify every physical layer

g.title: midground
g.text: MIDDLE-GROUND • nearer world layers
ATMOSPHERE → MIDGROUND_CLOUDS
Cloud cover may use overlapping clusters at Background and Middle-Ground depths; nearer clouds may cover the Sun and Moon

g.title: background->midground
g.text: absolute order

g.title: foreground
g.text: FOREGROUND
FOREGROUND_ARCHITECTURE → CANOPY → WINDOW_LIGHTS
Precipitation depth is owner choice; either placement follows both celestial cues

g.title: midground->foreground
g.text: absolute order

g.title: celestial
g.text: OWNER DIRECTION • CELESTIAL DEPTH
Outer space and stars form the backdrop; TIME_CUE (Sun) precedes LUNAR_CUE (Moon) inside Background.
The Moon may overlap the Sun. Atmosphere and closer cloud/world layers draw after both and may occlude them.

g.title: midground->celestial
g.text: recorded owner direction

g.title: pass
g.text: NAMED COMPOSITING PASSES
TIME_WASH and READOUT_QUIET_ZONE stay explicit passes, outside the physical depth groups.
Preserve their existing coverage and placement relative to the city layers; they do not reorder physical objects.

g.title: foreground->pass
g.text: separate pass semantics

g.title: rain
g.text: OWNER CHOICE • SINGLE PRECIPITATION FIELD / NEAR BUILDING
Moderate rain may fill the sky and span the scene with one field.
A. Middle-Ground: near buildings occlude the field.
B. Foreground: the field draws over near buildings (candidate current sequence); add no near/far split.

g.title: foreground->rain
g.text: confirm or revise field depth

g.title: invariants
g.text: PRESERVED INVARIANTS
Background < Middle-Ground < Foreground; no lower physical group paints above a higher group.

Inside Background: outer-space/stars → Sun → Moon → nearer background clouds/architecture. The Moon may overlay the Sun; all nearer atmosphere and world layers can occlude both. Keep local painter order inside each group. Preserve cloud-origin rain when visible clouds exist; preserve the no-cloud carried-rain field.
No change to weather evidence, exact selected instant, cue art, forecast text, or timeline behavior.

g.title: pass->invariants
g.text: pass contract

g.title: celestial->invariants
g.text: owner-directed overlap target

g.title: rain->invariants
g.text: selected overlap target

g.title: exit
g.text: OX-05 EXIT
Ordering assertions plus visually checked overlap cases; no cross-depth inversion.
Moderate-rain comparison: overlapping small-to-medium cloud clusters across Background and Middle-Ground, plus one scene-wide field; review Sun/Moon occlusion and near-building depth.
Installed visual evidence is still required for visual acceptance.

g.title: boundary
g.text: BOUNDARY
First City only. No semantic element registry (OX-06), second world, renderer extraction, new weather interpretation, or scene redesign.
Both boards are proposals; approval and package fingerprints will be recorded in cycle 144.
